column1: # Drugs that a pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in a disease gene makes
# risky, read by og pgx cpic-report (step 27 and CPIC_LOOKUP) with step 06's
# ClinVar hits (clinvar/<sample>_clinvar_hits.tsv). PharmCAT does not call
# these genes, so its report never names these drugs for them.
# The rows are the CPIC gene-drug pairs at level A, B or A/B whose gene is a
# disease gene outside PharmCAT and whose drug the variant makes risky
# (CPIC API pair_view, queried 2026-11-03; Pair_source is the query for the
# gene). Every pair here is provisional in CPIC (provisional true, no CPIC
# guideline): a gene with a CPIC guideline is one PharmCAT calls. A row needs
# a drug label that names the gene's disorder. Left out: NAGS with carglumic
# acid (the treatment, not a risk), ABL2 with valproic acid, and SCN1A with
# carbamazepine and phenytoin (no label or guideline names them; SCN1A also
# has gain-of-function disease variants, for which a warning against these
# drugs does not follow).
# Gene: the HGNC symbol, as ClinVar's GENEINFO writes it.
# Drug: the drug as CPIC names it.
# Names: the words a medication list may use for it, comma-separated, lower
# case. Every word of a medication line is matched, the second drug of a
# combination product too; a drug on the list is marked in the report.
# CPIC_level: the pair's CPIC level, printed as provisional.
# Note: what the label says.
# Label_source: the FDA label (DailyMed) the note quotes.
# Report_if: when a hit gives a WARNING. any: one variant does (POLG, where
# one variant is a known valproate risk, and the X-linked OTC and HPRT1,
# where a male has one copy and a female carrier can be affected).
# biallelic: the disorder is recessive, so the WARNING needs both copies
# changed (a homozygous or hemizygous genotype) or two variants in the gene;
# one heterozygous variant makes a carrier and gives a NOTE instead.
# cargo test -p og-pgx (tests/port_tests_pgx_cpic.rs) checks the shape of every row.
